learning: If slalom line_loss_events fall toward 0 and oval completions hold, the footprint was the sensing cause. If line loss does not fall, the outer span (x = ±0.06 m) is the likely limit. If line loss rises with 12 mm, the sensors are reading too little tape at the edges.
notes: Iteration 7 geometry with the sensor footprint reduced from 16 mm to 12 mm at the same positions. Controller held at iteration 7 values so the footprint is the only change.
rationale: Iteration 7 is the best design so far (303.8). It completed 14 of 20 oval runs, with progress 0.88 and max_error 0.048. Its s-bend and slalom still end off track, and slalom line loss is 0.3 per run. The Builder's proposal keeps every iteration 7 value and changes only the sensor footprint, from 16 mm to 12 mm. I keep the iteration 7 controller unchanged (kp 2.2, kd 0.5, ki 0.05, base_speed 1.4, last_direction, weights about 33 times x) so that the race isolates the footprint. Iteration 5 showed that the y = 0.02 m row with 16 mm sensors gave zero slalom line loss at 0.8 kg, while iteration 7 at 0.6 kg gave 0.3. This suggests the inertia change added slalom loss, and the footprint is the test. The footprint is the only geometry lever not yet varied at this inertia, so the test is clean. The risk is that a 12 mm footprint gives less tape coverage per sensor, so the outer sensors may read less and trigger line loss earlier. If that happens, the next step is a wider span at x = ±0.07 m, not a return to 16 mm. The track, wheels, mass and body stay fixed, so yaw and speed are unchanged.
